rubric_items.reason: All ten known REQs from req.md (REQ-1..REQ-10) are traced: S-1 has REQ-1..5, S-2 has REQ-6..7 and S-3 has REQ-8..10. There are no assumed REQs.
Each story has one user outcome: see the count, open the filtered list, or keep the rest of the dashboard unchanged. Each one can be delivered and tested on its own.
Every criterion uses Given/When/Then. S-1 AC5 and S-2 AC2 can only be checked against existing tile behaviour that is not in the inputs (U-1). AC4 only tests changing from Today.
Every value comes from the intent: the No-shows title, the Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days periods, and the Completed and Cancelled tiles. No limits are invented.
Terms are clear and match the intent and glossary. The body mirrors the frontmatter, with some phrases shortened.

findings.text: The split carries only the counting half of req Q-01. The open point about whether the link uses the period's dates, which affects S-2 AC2 (REQ-7), was dropped, so the unknown that S-2 depends on is not recorded.

cites.quote: and link with the period's dates, so No-shows can copy them exactly?
then the appointment list is filtered to that selected period.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend U-1 and Q-01 to cover the link format as well as the counting, and note that S-2 AC2 is checked against the existing tiles' links.

findings.text: S-1 AC4 only tests changing from Today to the other periods. REQ-5 says any change of period updates the count, so changing from Last 7 days or Last 30 days is not tested.

cites.quote: Given the period is Today, when staff change it to Last 7 days or Last 30 days
Changing the period `updates` the No-shows count

findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC4 as: Given any selected period, when staff change it to another period, then the count updates.

cites.quote: The dashboard has a tile titled `No-shows`.
The selected period is one of `Today`, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.
No-shows are counted the same way as the `Completed and Cancelled` tiles count their appointments.
A past appointment the patient did not attend, closed instead of staying Scheduled.
